players.product: ultra-high-purity germanium, gallium, indium and tellurium; germanium substrates

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO): revenue increased 28% to $122.4 million vs Q2 2025; H1 revenue $240.3 million, up 30%, reflecting higher volumes in renewable energy, a more favorable product mix in space power and higher volumes of bismuth-based products. Adjusted gross margin $37 million or 30.3% of sales (vs $33 million or 34.6%); H1 adjusted gross margin 32.6%. Adjusted EBITDA up 10% to $26.6 million; H1 $55.8 million (CEO: growth of 24%). Net earnings $19.7 million or $0.22 per share (vs $15.2 million, $0.17). Net debt $23.7 million at end of June vs $50.3 million at end of 2025; net debt to adjusted EBITDA 0.21 times. CEO: overall, volume is the main factor behind the revenue increase.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $122.4 million (+28%); H1 $240.3 million (+30%); adjusted gross margin 30.3%; adjusted EBITDA $26.6 million (+10%); net earnings $19.7 million

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: 2026 full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $100 to $105 million reaffirmed (H1 $55.8 million, slightly above the midpoint), reflecting continued revenue growth and higher gross margin dollars in H2 with a prudent view of input costs. CFO: margins expected under additional near-term pressure from higher metal input and chemical costs, to be partially recovered (not 100%) with at least a two-quarter lag; Q2 gross margin is a good projection for H2 within a one percentage point band. CFO: higher metal costs and the operational difficulties (unplanned equipment maintenance) had a fairly equal impact on Q2 gross margin; CEO agreed the maintenance part was about half of the decline and called it temporary, with no expected impact on H2 shipments.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA $100 to $105 million; H2 gross margin within one percentage point of Q2 (30.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Specialty Semiconductors (CFO): revenue up 25% to $89.2 million, primarily on higher renewable-energy volumes; adjusted gross margin 30.2% (vs 32.7%) on higher metal input costs and lower operating efficiency; adjusted EBITDA up 16% to $22.1 million. Backlog remains at the maximum level of 365 days per the company's definition, with effective backlog continuing to well surpass the 12-month mark. CEO: terrestrial renewable energy had record quarterly revenue, reflecting the key customer's (not named) continuous expansion and the company's position as a critical supplier in its value chain; 2026 is a bigger volume increase, and 2027 and 2028 are also increased volume but on a smaller scale.

Space solar power (AZUR SPACE, III-V multi-junction solar cells for LEO, MEO and GEO). CEO: significant new contract awards secured in H1 and a record level of bids by dollar value in Q2; H1 bids at least twice the dollar amount of the same period last year, highly diversified by client and constellation/satellite program. Asked about the AZUR order book, CEO: 2026 is sold out, 2027 is sold out; assessing opportunities to increase capacity further for 2027 and working out scenarios for 2028 to 2030. CEO: data centers in space are still under development, probably a couple of years before launches; none of the bids are known to be specific to data centers. A VLEO product line is possible but nothing confirmed.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 bids at least twice prior-year dollar amount; 2026 and 2027 sold out

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex. CEO: equipment is being pushed close to its limit while new equipment (new designs) and a large number of new employees are integrated, almost equally across terrestrial and space; capacity is added in line with contracts, correlating order taking with capacity investments; expansion plans remain on plan. PP&E capex $16.6 million year to date (CFO). CEO: on a net cash-out basis (some U.S. equipment supported by a government grant) the 2026 capex expectation remains valid, with equipment brought on earlier to address 2027 volume requirements. U.S. germanium refining capacity expansion (grant-supported), CEO: progressing as per plan, expanding the existing building, equipment arriving and more ordered; completion will take probably close to a year and a half to two years, adding capacity gradually quarter to quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: PP&E capex $16.6 million year to date; germanium refining expansion close to a year and a half to two years to complete

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the CDSC line in Montreal is planned to start running in the second half, most likely around the end of Q3 2026; products are being pre-qualified, with ramp-up and formal qualification later in H2 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: start most likely around the end of Q3 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Performance Materials (CFO): revenue up 38% to $33.2 million on higher volumes of bismuth-based products; adjusted gross margin 30.9% (vs 41.1%), reflecting the anticipated normalization plus higher metal input and chemical costs; adjusted EBITDA up 7% to $8.5 million; backlog 99 days of annualized revenue. CEO: H1 is historically stronger than H2 as clients reduce inventory at year-end; year-to-date gross margin could be used as the H2 assumption, with chemical costs (nitric acid, caustic soda) still rising.

CEO views: customers increasingly value secure, reliable Western supply chains, particularly in renewable energy, space, security and advanced technologies. On perovskite, the strategy is to focus on the individual elements rather than encapsulation technology; outside China it is still early stage as a tandem material, and meaningful commercial volume is most likely a year or two away (terrestrial applications far more advanced than space).
